features.text: The patient has been experiencing numbness and tingling in both hands for a few weeks.
The symptoms began after a car wreck in December when the patient broke both wrists.
The numbness and tingling have worsened over the last month.
The patient has mild stiffness in her neck, which occurred during the accident and was diagnosed as a contusion.
The neck stiffness has been present since the accident and is not associated with headaches, dizziness, or visual changes.
The patient has not had any imaging studies for her neck or wrists since the accident.
The patient had a CT brain with and without contrast on February 5th, which showed no metastatic disease or acute intercranial abnormalities.
The patient is willing to undergo cervical spine imaging (e.g., MRI) and X-rays of the wrists if recommended.
The numbness and tingling in the right hand affect the middle and ring finger up to the forearm.
The numbness and tingling in the left hand affect the pinky and ring finger, not the middle finger.
The patient experiences soreness and weakness in her hands, especially when using them.
The tingling is more noticeable at night and comes and goes throughout the day.
The patient has noticed worsening numbness and tingling in the right hand over the past month.
The patient has difficulty with fine motor tasks such as buttoning shirts and holding small objects.
The patient has experienced some difficulty with hand strength and coordination, including dropping objects.
The patient has not undergone any neurological evaluations such as EMG or nerve conduction studies.
The patient is open to undergoing EMG and nerve conduction studies if recommended.
